newsitem.title: TURKEY: Power slips away from Turkish Islamist PM Erbakan.
newsitem.headline: Power slips away from Turkish Islamist PM Erbakan.

text.p: Necmettin Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, wrapped up talks with his coalition allies on Wednesday before heading for the presidential palace where he was expected to resign.

The last-minute bargaining, to finalise a planned transfer of power to Tansu Ciller, Erbakan's pro-Western deputy, came just hours before the expiration of a midnight deadline (2100 GMT) imposed by Ciller's conservative True Path Party.

The two partners, who have watched their parliamentary majority melt away before an anti-Islamist onslaught led by the army brass, were joined by the leader of a far-right splinter party that has pledged to back the new government.
"I will take the agreement which we have reached to the president," Erbakan said after a meeting with Ciller and rightist leader Muhsin Yazicioglu.
He said he would meet Demirel at 6.30 p.m. (1530 GMT).
Ciller, who is also foreign minister, told reporters at the same briefing that Erbakan's year-old government would come to an end "shortly".
But Erbakan, a 70-year-old veteran of Turkish politics, made no direct reference to resigning during the news conference.
Investors on Turkey's volatile stock exchange likewise proved unwilling to commit themselves. The main index closed almost unchanged.
"Serious buying was hindered by uncertainty over who would be given the duty to form a government," Hakan Aksoy of Alfa Securities told Reuters.

The proposed transfer of power, which still faces a host of procedural and political obstacles, was announced earlier this month in a bid to defuse the crisis with the military, which accuses Erbakan of fostering Islamic activism.
Under the plan, Ciller would then take the country to early polls, a tactic Erbakan has promised the party faithful will allow him to return to power with an expanded mandate.

The military, which has toppled three governments in the last four decades, has publically pledged its readiness to turn back any threat to Turkey's secular order "by force of arms" -- tough talk that has alarmed close ally the United States.

The mainstream media and business elite have also fed the current anti-Islamist hysteria, sparking enough defections among MPs and ministers from among Ciller's conservatives to cost the coalition a majority in the 550-seat parliament.

Even Welfare, traditionally a bastion of party discipline, has seen its number of deputies fall, depriving it of valuable votes in the revamped coalition's bid for a confidence vote. Two radical Welfare MPs quit the party on Wednesday.
The last-ditch negotiations came just ahead of a True Path deadline, largely at the urging of Ciller's restive backbenchers.

"We have given Welfare until 2400 (2100 GMT). This is our last date and we will give no concessions on it. If Erbakan doesn't resign we will do what is needed," the Hurriyet daily quoted True Path senior MP Mehmet Golhan as saying.
Other True Path officals confirmed the threat.
Erbakan's tenure, now apparently in its final hours, saw a harried leader effectively blocked by army pressure from introducing Islamist reforms and building bridges to Turkey's Moslem neighbours.
Erbakan presided at the weekend over the founding summit in Istanbul of the Developing-Eight (D-8) Moslem nations, a water-down version of his campaign pledge to head a new Islamic power bloc.

But he has been helpless to limit Turkey's role in NATO and to stop growing military ties with Israel that have angered the Arabs. Five Turkish navy vessels docked in an Israeli port on Monday in defiance of the prime minister's pro-Arab stance.
